title: Open job PR early at verification start so CI caches during verify
summary: Retry: when verification starts, athena go pushes the candidate and opens or updates the job's PR through the host seam, with no merge, so CI fills the cache in that PR's scope. Failures are non-fatal. A missing or non-GitHub origin skips quietly, so existing CLI tests stay green. Land reuses the PR and sets link.head to the landing commit before the head check.

defaults_applied.how: Behavior criteria run cargo test, clippy and fmt --check.
Criteria check the push, open and non-fatal behavior, not just wiring.
One focused change on the early-PR step.
Criteria name commands the verifier can run.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Goal: faster landings for the maintainer; the retry fixes the earlier plan's gaps (existing CLI tests, runner source, link.head).
The early step skips quietly when origin is missing or not GitHub; this keeps lifecycle.rs green without editing it.
Opening the PR early, not just pushing, follows the user's cache-scoping correction.
Not read: repository files; paths are inferred from the earlier job's findings.

acceptance_criteria.text: A fake-host test shows that when verification starts, the candidate is pushed to the job's PR branch and the PR is opened or updated via Remote::push and PrHost::open_pr before verification completes, with no merge call. Run: cargo test -p athena-core.
A fake-host test shows that a failing early push or early open_pr leaves the job's outcome identical to the no-failure case. Run: cargo test -p athena-core.

A test shows land still pushes the landing commit to the same branch, reuses the early PR (no second open_pr), sets link.head to the landing commit after the lease-pinned replace (via check_replace) and before the head check, and merges guarded with the landing commit. Run: cargo test -p athena-core.

A test runs go with no GitHub origin and shows the early step is silent: no output line contains 'warning'. The existing CLI lifecycle tests still pass. Only failures after the host is known print a warning. Run: cargo test --workspace.
cargo test --workspace, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets and cargo fmt --check all pass with no warnings. Each new test fails without the new behavior.
The production early-push implementation builds its own gh runner (GhCli) so the Athena::go signature and CLI call sites stay unchanged.
CHANGELOG.md says that verification start opens or updates the job's PR so CI caches by fingerprint, that it never merges, and that failures are non-fatal.

out_of_scope: Changing the Athena::go signature or CLI call sites
